subject: Intermittent app-to-db drops — transit routing + SNAT suspect
snippet: Acme reports intermittent app->DB failures over private link; initial analysis points to TGW route leaking + SNAT asymmetry and MTU issues. Action items and maintenance coordinate.
messages:
From: Nate Brooks <nate.b@acme-corp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME NetOps <netops@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: App -> DB intermittent failures over private link

Jordan —

We started seeing intermittent failures this morning in Prod: Pods in our app VPC are intermittently failing health checks to the DB (hosted in our private VPC behind an internal ALB). Symptoms: short TCP connect timeouts, SYN retries, and a surge of RSTs seen by the app side. The issue lasts ~3-10 minutes then clears.

Topology: App VPC -> TGW -> Private VPC (DB). We recently added a partner VPC via the transit gateway (CloudPartner) last week.

I ran a quick tcpdump on the app host and attached a short pcap. Also attached an export of the TGW route tables.

Attachments: pcap_snip_tcpdump_2027-03-16.pcap (pcap), route_table_export.txt (text)

Can you help triage? This is impacting a small % of traffic but at scale the errors are visible in our SLO dashboards.

Thanks,
Nate Brooks
NetOps — Acme Corp

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Nate Brooks <nate.b@acme-corp.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:02:12 -0700
Subject: Re: App -> DB intermittent failures over private link

Thanks Nate —

Got your pcap and route dump, appreciate the details. Looping in Rishi (networking) and Vivek (private deploy infra). Initial hypotheses:

- Transit gateway route propagation/overlap from CloudPartner causing an asymmetric return path (TGW route leak into the DB VPC)
- SNAT behavior on the app side (or on an intermediate firewall) causing packets to be sourced differently on return, leading to state mismatch
- MTU/path-fragmentation causing SYN retries (less likely but seen on OVS-based on-prem connectors)

Quick asks to help narrow down:
1) Can you capture a 1s-2m full three-way handshake time series (SYN->SYN/ACK->ACK) with packet-level timestamps from both the app host and the DB side?
2) Can you share the TGW route table IDs and the attachment IDs for the two VPCs (app & db)?
3) Any recent changes to SNAT rules, NAT gateways, or edge appliances in the last 7 days?

I'll look at the route dump now. If this looks like route leaking we'll propose a temporary route preference and SNAT mitigation to avoid dropping connections.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Nate Brooks <nate.b@acme-corp.com>
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 11:30:45 -0700
Subject: Re: App -> DB intermittent failures over private link

On Tue, Mar 16, 2027 at 09:02 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Got your pcap and route dump, appreciate the details. Looping in Rishi (networking) and Vivek (private deploy infra). Initial hypotheses: ...

Quick pass on the route dump and a few notes: attached a cleaned route_table_export.txt and a short OVS config snippet I asked for from a similar on-prem connector. Things I see:

- The TGW route table shows propagated routes from the partner attachment pointing at the same /24 that contains the DB subnet. That creates a second path for return traffic from the DB to the app (likely asymmetric).
- There's no explicit route priority set between the two propagated routes — TGW chooses attachments by propagation order and attachments can flap during partner maintenance.
- If the DB responds via the partner path while the app connection state expects the return via the original attachment, TCP state will break (RST/SYN retry pattern).

Actionable short-term mitigations:
1) Add a static route in the DB VPC route table pointing at the direct attachment (preferred) for the app prefix to force symmetric return.
2) If you have a NAT gateway or stateful firewall that performs SNAT on the app egress, ensure that the SNAT pool is consistent across both attachments or add a MASQ at the app side to avoid mismatched source IPs.
3) If on-prem OVS connectors are used, clamp MSS to 1400 on tunnel endpoints — I'm attaching config-ovs-mtu.txt for reference.

Attachments: route_table_export.txt (cleaned), config-ovs-mtu.txt (text)

I'll keep digging. Vivek, any infra-level constraints we should be aware of for applying a static route in a live maintenance window?

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Network Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: Nate Brooks <nate.b@acme-corp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME NetOps <netops@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 13:10:03 -0700
Subject: Re: App -> DB intermittent failures over private link

Thanks Rishi — good notes. We captured a slightly longer pcap from the DB side; I'm attaching a 20s snippet. Observations:

- We see SYN arrive at DB, DB replies with SYN/ACK, then we sometimes see the SYN/ACK forwarded to a different next hop and the app never ACKs (leading to retries).
- There are cases where MSS is 1460 and subsequent fragmentation/ICMP needed signals are not arriving at the app side — possibly blocked or lost on the partner path.
- No SNAT changes on our side in the last 14 days; partner did a config push last week.

Attachments: pcap_snip_tcpdump_2027-03-16.pcap (full db-side snippet)

If TGW route reuse is flapping, I can open a partner incident but we need a short-term fix. Can we try the static route suggestion + a temporary security group rule to allow the ephemeral port range (32768-61000) from the DB to app?

—Nate
ACME NetOps
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Nate Brooks <nate.b@acme-corp.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: CloudPartner Support <support@cloudpvt.example>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 16:40:12 -0700
Subject: Re: App -> DB intermittent failures over private link

Thanks everyone for the data. Quick summary and plan to resolve ASAP: 

Summary (root causes likely):
- Transit GW route propagation from CloudPartner is overlapping the DB prefix, causing occasional asymmetric return paths when partner attachment becomes preferred.
- Asymmetric return + potential SNAT mismatch and missing ICMP 'fragmentation needed' makes TCP handshakes fail intermittently.
- OVS-based connectors (if present in partner path) may exacerbate MTU issues.

Immediate action items (short-term fixes, low risk):
1) Acme: Add a host-specific static route in the DB VPC route table for the app subnet pointing at the local attachment (forces symmetric return). This is reversible and low blast radius.
2) Acme: Temporarily open ephemeral port range 32768-61000 in the DB security group for the app prefix to avoid connection drops while we stabilize routing.
3) CloudPartner: Please verify you are not doing SNAT for the DB prefix and ensure ICMP (type 3 code 4) is not being filtered on the partner path.
4) Redwood (Rishi/Vivek): Prepare a recommendation for a durable fix — options: TGW route table priority/filters, an explicit static route strategy, or enforce egress SNAT consistency. Also prepare a quick runbook for rolling back the static route if side effects occur.

Next steps: Nate, can you apply item (1) as a test and confirm if the window clears? CloudPartner, please acknowledge and check SNAT/ICMP. Jordan/Rishi/Vivek and I will stand by.

Attachments referenced: route_table_export.txt, config-ovs-mtu.txt, pcap_snip_tcpdump_2027-03-16.pcap

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Director, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference
